cards.headline: 30 people evacuated, 1 person taken to hospital after fire breaks out in Bukit Batok coffee shop
bullets: A fire at a Bukit Batok coffee shop on Oct 11 morning caused 30 people to be evacuated.
One person was taken to the hospital after the fire.
The blaze involved three food stalls on the ground floor of the coffee shop.
The cause of the fire is currently being investigated by the SCDF.

cards.headline: URA flags ‘persistent trend’ of suspected cases of unauthorised works in residential units
bullets: URA is seeing many reports of illegal home renovations like adding lofts or enclosing patios.
About 90% of suspected illegal works found by URA were confirmed to have violations.
These illegal changes can affect building safety, insurance claims, and property value.
URA warns that owners who don't comply with enforcement notices may face court action.

cards.headline: PCF Sparkletots to double staff development spending to $20m, ease teachers’ admin workload
bullets: PCF Sparkletots will spend $20 million more on teacher training over three years.
Teachers will get help with admin work through a new central system.
Mother tongue classes will be offered in all PCF Sparkletots centres if needed.
PCF Sparkletots will share teaching tips for kids with different learning needs.

cards.headline: Malaysian low-cost carrier Firefly cancels all flights between Seletar and Subang airports amid haze
bullets: Firefly cancelled flights between Seletar and Subang from Oct 10 to 12 due to haze.
The cancellations were a safety precaution because of low visibility.
Affected passengers can switch to Malaysia Airlines flights or get a full refund.
Singapore’s air quality hit a high of 192 on Oct 9 due to haze.

cards.headline: Legoland Malaysia Resort’s new rooms, Singapore Polo Club’s charity carnival, student art exhibition
bullets: Legoland Malaysia Resort has 31 new Lego City-themed hotel rooms.
The Singapore Polo Club is holding a charity carnival on Oct 17.
Enjoy pony rides and a show-jumping demonstration at the carnival.
An art exhibition called Interplay is showing works by young students.
The free Interplay exhibition runs until Oct 25 at Lewin Terrace.

cards.headline: Malaysian low-cost carrier Firefly cancels all flights between Subang, Seletar airports due to haze
bullets: Firefly cancelled all flights between Subang and Seletar airports until Monday.
The cancellations are due to the haze affecting air quality.
Affected passengers can get refunds or be moved to Malaysia Airlines flights.
Air quality in Malaysia and Singapore remained unhealthy.

cards.headline: Singapore to roll out haze subsidies at GP clinics, polyclinics from Oct 12
bullets: Haze treatment subsidies start Oct 12 at clinics and polyclinics.
Singaporeans pay max S$10 for haze-related sickness at these places.
Seniors and kids get cheaper treatment, paying no more than S$5.
Over 1,000 clinics are expected to join the subsidy scheme.

cards.headline: Air quality remains unhealthy across Singapore amid haze
bullets: Air quality is unhealthy with haze expected to continue.
The 24-hour PSI is forecast to stay unhealthy to very unhealthy.
Moderate haze is seen over Singapore and nearby regions.
Government agencies are ready to act if air quality worsens.
Schools might close if the air quality becomes hazardous.

cards.headline: She turned her kids’ old clothes into keepsakes – now it’s a thriving home business
bullets: A mum turns kids' old clothes into stuffed toys and quilts, starting a successful home business.
Her business, Patchwork Handmade Keepsakes, makes keepsakes from baby clothes to school uniforms.
Prices for a keepsake bear start at S$85, and a quilt starts at S$120.
She now makes about as much money as her old admin job before she was laid off.

cards.headline: Odette’s longtime wine director Vincent Tan is leaving after 10 years to join Park90
bullets: Odette's wine director Vincent Tan is leaving after 10 years.
He will become Park90's new group wine director as it expands.
Park90 has moved to Pan Pacific Orchard and offers over 1,000 wine labels.
Tan wants Park90's wine programme to be shaped by personality and discovery.

cards.headline: Australia home auction clearance rate stuck below 50% for second week
bullets: Less than half of Australian homes up for auction sold for the second week running.
Higher interest rates and tax changes are hurting buyer demand in Australia.
Australian home prices are back to where they were a year ago.
The number of home auctions in Australia is the lowest since 2020.

cards.headline: ‘Natural’ fit: F1 team Williams ties up with Twice’s Tzuyu, anime Dandadan to reach new audiences
bullets: F1 team Williams is teaming up with K-pop star Tzuyu and anime Dandadan.
Tzuyu will sing a theme song for the collaboration, out in early 2027.
The partnership aims to connect F1 fans with anime and K-pop audiences.
Merchandise like shirts and bags are already available for the collaboration.

cards.headline: 2026 Mini John Cooper Works review: Uniquely fun, but one rival could spoil the party
bullets: The new Mini John Cooper Works (JCW) car offers a fun, go-kart like driving experience.
It has a powerful 2.0-litre turbo engine with 231 horsepower and 380 Nm of torque.
The car features a sporty design with racing-inspired interior touches.
Despite its fun factor, the JCW is basic with limited cabin storage and a small boot.
The Volkswagen Golf GTI is a more practical and comfortable alternative.

cards.headline: Steven Pan’s Silks Hotel Group looks beyond hotels for next phase of growth
bullets: Silks Hotel Group is exploring becoming a hospitality holding company, not just hotels.
They are looking at buying businesses like travel agencies and restaurants too.
The group is negotiating to buy a historic hotel in San Francisco.
Silks Hotel Group also wants to bring its Regent brand back to Singapore and Bangkok.

cards.headline: Premier League returns after three-week break as Manchester City saga rumbles on
bullets: Manchester City faces serious financial charges and appeals the verdict.
The English Premier League resumes after a three-week break.
League leaders Manchester City play Liverpool at Anfield this weekend.
Arsenal aims to bounce back after a recent loss.
Manchester United and Tottenham Hotspur are struggling at the bottom of the table.

cards.headline: MOE to consider closing schools & postponing exams if next-day PSI forecast exceeds 300: Desmond Lee
bullets: Schools may close and exams be postponed if the haze forecast goes above 300.
Decisions on school closures will be announced by 8pm the day before.
Lessons and exams will continue indoors with air purifiers for now.
N95 masks will be distributed if the haze reaches very unhealthy levels.

cards.headline: Actors from S'pore film, The Sandbox, tries to surprise moviegoers at screening, finds only 7 people in cinema
bullets: Only seven people showed up for a surprise screening of local film The Sandbox.
Cast members, including Nathan Hartono, attended the showing.
Hartono noted the low turnout reflects the challenges of releasing independent films in Singapore.
The film follows a stunt school that gets popular after a Marvel rumour.
The director urged support for local films in cinemas, not just waiting for streaming.

cards.headline: Chinese tourist has LV bag allegedly stolen at Gardens By The Bay, asks passerby for directions, turns out to be thief
bullets: A tourist's Louis Vuitton bag was stolen at Gardens By The Bay on Oct. 5.
The tourist tracked his missing bag using wireless earbuds inside.
He asked a passerby for directions, who turned out to be the thief.
The tourist recovered his bag within 20 minutes, but lost cash and other items.
Police confirmed a report was lodged and investigations are ongoing.

cards.headline: This New Escape Room By Mediacorp 987 & Xcape SG Turns A Radio Station Into A Horror Movie
bullets: A new radio-themed horror escape room is open until November 1, 2026.
It's called 'Signal Hijacked: The Purge Protocol' and features live actors.
You have 75 minutes to solve puzzles and survive the night.
Tickets cost $39.90 for standard times and $45.90 for peak hours.
